identity.title: Gas Gaps in the Protoplanetary Disk around the Young Protostar HL Tau

paper_type_evidence.quote: The HL Tau data analyzed here were retrieved from the public data release of the ALMA Science Verification observations (project code: 2011.0.00015.SV).

evidence.quote: HL Tau is a Class I–II protostellar source located in the northern part of the L1551 region in the Taurus molecular cloud at a distance of $\sim$140 pc (cite: Hayashi09).
HL Tau is a Class I–II protostellar source located in the northern part of the L1551 region in the Taurus molecular cloud at a distance of $\sim$140 pc (cite: Hayashi09).

question.value: Do the millimeter continuum gaps in the HL Tau disk have counterparts in the HCO+ (1-0) gas, and what do the gas gap widths and depths imply for their origin?

evidence.quote: we report the radial intensity profiles and reconstructed intensity map of the HCO$^+$ (1–0) emission in the disk around HL Tau at a high angular resolution of $\sim$0.07$''$, revealing the counterparts of the continuum gaps in the gas component.
public data release of the ALMA Science Verification observations (project code: 2011.0.00015.SV)
HCO$^+$ (1–0; 89.188526 GHz) and CO (1–0; 115.271202 GHz) image cubes
HCO$^+$ (1–0; 89.188526 GHz) and CO (1–0; 115.271202 GHz) image cubes
The angular resolutions of the HCO$^+$ and CO images are $\sim$0.1$''$ $\times$ 0.05$''$ and $\sim$0.07$''$ $\times$ 0.04$''$, respectively
their noise levels are $\sim$2 and $\sim$6 mJy Beam$^{-1}$ per channel.

analysis_steps.goal: Azimuthally averaged radial HCO+ intensity profile

method.value: Deprojected with i=47 deg, PA=138 deg; bins of half beam (~0.035''); pixels within ±45 deg of major axis; integrate 2-12 km/s excluding absorption and ±1 sigma channels

evidence.quote: only the pixels within $\pm$45$^\circ$ of the major axis were included in azimuthal averaging

key_parameters.value: uncertainty = sqrt(N_int) x sigma x dv

evidence.quote: The uncertainty of the integrated intensity at each radial bin was estimated as $\sqrt{N_{\rm int}} \times \sigma \times dv$
assuming the intensity distribution is axisymmetric

validation.value: gap hints seen on both sides of the disk

evidence.quote: the hints of the gaps at $\sim$30 AU and $\sim$70 AU are seen on the both sides of the disk

analysis_steps.goal: Derive continuum optical depth and HCO+ column density

method.value: T from CO brightness temperature without continuum subtraction; tau_3mm from radiative transfer; correct HCO+ for continuum optical depth; column density from Mangum & Shirley formula

evidence.quote: The temperature profile ($T$) is adopted to be the radial profile of the brightness temperature of the CO emission without continuum subtraction

assumptions.value: dust and gas thermally coupled with the same temperature; HCO+ thermalized; CO+continuum optically thick

evidence.quote: we assume that the dust grains and the gas are thermally well coupled and have the same temperature, and that the HCO$^+$ gas is thermalized
its 1$\sigma$ uncertainty was estimated by propagating the uncertainties in $T$ and $T_{\rm b,3mm}$

method.value: Power law fit near each gap, subtract, Gaussian fit to gap for FWHM and central column density; contrast vs power law

evidence.quote: we first fitted a power-law function to the column densities only at the radial bins near the gap
We repeated this fitting process for a 10,000 times
Assuming the HCO$^+$ abundance does not vary across the gaps

fitting.value: Monte Carlo resampling of radii and densities; Gaussian fits to parameter distributions give best-fit and 1 sigma

evidence.quote: the centers and standard deviations of the fitted Gaussian functions were adopted as the best-fit values and the 1$\sigma$ uncertainties
the 10,000 iterations is sufficient to converge

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate planet masses from gap depth

method.value: Kanagawa15 gap formula using derived temperature and depths

evidence.quote: lead to planet masses of $\sim$0.8 $M_J$ at $\sim$28 AU and $\sim$2.1 $M_J$ at $\sim$69 AU
assuming the viscosity $\alpha$ of 0.001
using the tasks in Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA)
Both HCO$^+$ gaps have similar FWHM widths of $\sim$14$\pm$7 AU.

findings_qualitative.value: The central HCO+ cavity is likely due to high optical depth of the 3 mm continuum, not gas depletion.

evidence.quote: the presence of the central cavity is likely due to the high optical depth of the 3 mm continuum emission and not the depletion of the HCO$^+$ gas.

claims.result: Gaps at ~28 and ~69 AU; inner coincides with D2, outer overlaps D5/D6 and B5
claims.finding: Gas and dust are depleted at D2, D5, D6

evidence.quote: Two gaps at radii of $\sim$28 AU and $\sim$69 AU and a central cavity are identified in the radial intensity profile.

claims.experiment: Compare gas gap widths and depths with the gap formula
claims.result: Widths ~14 AU, depths 2.4 and 5.0, masses ~0.8 and 2.1 MJ
claims.finding: Consistent with sub-Jovian planets, constrains dust-only models

evidence.quote: These results are consistent with the expectation from the gaps opened by forming (sub-)Jovian mass planets

why_this_method.value: Azimuthal averaging to raise S/N because no clear detection above 3 sigma in the cube

evidence.quote: we performed azimuthal averaging on the image cube to enhance the S/N ratio

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO snow line origin of the outer gap is possible but needs detailed calculations; less likely for the inner gap.

evidence.quote: Thus, this scenario is less possible to interpret the presence of the inner HCO$^+$ gap.

limitations_admitted.value: Column density biased by poorly constrained dust and gas temperature profiles.

evidence.quote: the overall HCO$^+$ column density profile remains biased by the not as well constrained radial temperature profiles of the dust and the gas.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas temperature from CO brightness temperature may differ from dust midplane temperature
Absorption by foreground cloud affects the integrated intensity
Gap widths are comparable to the beam, so uncertainties are large
